The PSNR in dB against the image under the scanner blur alone. Each scan is a clustered-dot screen of the image, with the period in pixels and the angle given, blurred with a Gaussian of sigma 1.2 as a scanner would. Both images are 160 by 160 pixels. By PSNR, descreening with the defaults stays a little behind a Gaussian blur of sigma 2 on three of the four scans. The dots of a binary screen also leave broadband noise, which no notch can remove, while the blur removes some of it. On the disks and the Siemens star without a screen, the filter changes no pixel at all, since their spectra hold lines and rings, not isolated peaks.
